title: board_debug.jsonl
description: One JSON object per line, appended by tools/bma_debug_rx.py from the board daemon's debug stream (bma-audiod on the board: FPGA meters, the DSP raw-receive level monitor, @health housekeeping, daemon status). Every record carries `host_t` (PC Unix seconds at receipt) and `type`. The file rotates at 64 MB. Receivers MUST ignore unknown fields and SHOULD tolerate unknown `type` values (the contract checker flags them as drift so the contract is updated).

hex8_or_empty.description: Eight hex digits (a big-endian float32), or the empty string when the board could not read the sensor (28 health records on 2026-10-11 16:01-16:22); the matching *_c field is then null.

host_t.description: PC wall clock at receipt, Unix seconds (float).

meter.description: FPGA meter registers (BMAM datagram). `vals` maps a 2-hex-digit selector to a 4-hex-digit register value. `zero` is the datagram's flags bit 0.

ms.description: Board uptime in milliseconds at sampling.

monitor.description: One line of the DSP raw-receive level monitor `t dsp slot meansq peak` (board monitor): DSPs 4-9 times slots 0-6 = 42 lines per sweep. Levels are relative to 24-bit full scale (2^23): peak_dbfs = 20 log10(peak/2^23), rms_dbfs = 10 log10(meansq/2^46). SLOT 4 IS NOT AN AUDIO CHANNEL: its raw values sit near full scale and the collector deliberately reports rms_dbfs null for it. rms_dbfs/peak_dbfs are also null when meansq/peak is 0. A line that does not parse as five integers is kept as the `raw` shape (type, seq, line, host_t only).

seq.description: Datagram sequence (all lines of one datagram share it).

t.description: Board-side tick from the monitor line (NOT wall clock).

then.description: Parsed shape: the moment any parsed field is present, all of them must be.

health.description: Board housekeeping, one JSON object per ~60 s from the board (the daemon tails /fwlog/board_health.log, tag @health). The board emits `k`; the collector adds `type`, `seq`, `temp_local_c`, `temp_remote_c` (float32 decoded from the *_hex fields, null if undecodable) and `host_t`. `eth0` is five comma-separated counters, `eth1` three (as the board emits them).

fpga.description: FPGA registers as 4-hex-digit strings. ea = safety mute (0000 = unmuted). f0/f2 are runtime state, not configuration.

d_state.description: Processes in uninterruptible sleep; a non-zero value that persists means a wedged SPI user.

status.description: Daemon status. `json` is a JSON-ENCODED STRING (double encoded) holding the inner object described by $defs/status_inner; the contract checker validates the inner object too.

status_inner.description: Only `state` is guaranteed: right after the daemon starts it reports just {"state":"starting"}; every later status carries all five fields.

state.description: Daemon mode: `starting`, then `meters_only` (the production default, no media path on the board) or a media mode.

subs.description: Subscribers currently attached to the daemon.

health_unparsed.description: A line that started with `@health ` but did not parse as JSON. In practice the line is a few hundred NUL bytes followed by the intact JSON object (a torn write at log rotation/truncation); about 2% of health lines. Consumers may recover it by stripping NULs and parsing from the first `{`. The record is a known degraded kind, not drift.
